grading_standard: All requested material parts required; abstention partial, contradiction incorrect. Grade semantics independent of support label. Unsupported guesses separately flagged. No cross-answer borrowing.

grades.question: How is the Conflict deck built, and what happens to unused Conflict cards?
grades.expected: Shuffle all four III cards at the bottom, five randomly dealt of nine II cards above, one randomly dealt of three I cards on top: ten total. Return unused cards to the box without looking.

observed.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down on the bottom; shuffle the 9 II cards and deal 5 face down above them; shuffle the 3 I cards and deal 1 face down on top. Return unused I and II cards unseen to the box.
observed.evidence: Setup: face-down Conflict Deck construction.

grades.reason: Both reproduce all deck tiers, random selection, order and unseen return.

grades.question: What are the starting score, Agents, troops and water for a human in a four-player game versus a three-player game?
grades.expected: Four players start at 1 VP; three at 0. Each has two Agents on Leader and third beside board, three troops in garrison with remaining nine in supply, and one water.

observed.answer: In four-player play a human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play, at 0 VP. Each starts with 2 Agents on the Leader and a third/Swordmaster beside the board; 3 troops in the garrison and 9 in supply; and 1 water.
observed.evidence: Setup steps 6 and Human component layout.

grades.reason: Both give the differing starting VP and all requested Agent, troop and water quantities and locations.

grades.question: Can you Reveal with Agents left, and can you later take an Agent turn in the same round? What cards supply Reveal effects and where do all played cards go?
grades.expected: May Reveal early; no more turns this phase after Reveal. Only cards remaining in hand and just revealed supply Reveal effects, not Agent-turn cards. Clean Up puts all Agent and Reveal cards in discard pile.

observed.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but once you Reveal your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed for that Reveal turn, not Agent-played cards. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: Player Turns and Reveal Turn.

grades.reason: Both permit early Reveal, prohibit later turns, restrict Reveal effects and give discard destination.

grades.question: May an Agent-turn card effect provide resources to pay the destination entry cost? How many Agents can one card send, and can a card without Agent icons be used?
grades.expected: Entry costs paid immediately before any card or space effects; cannot use later gains to pay entry. One card sends one Agent using one matching icon. No-icon card cannot be played on an Agent turn.

observed.answer: A Plot Intrigue may be played before placing the Agent and resources it grants before entry can pay the cost; effects from the played Agent card or destination occur too late to pay that same cost. One card sends one Agent using one chosen icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn; it may only be revealed.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: Plot Intrigue timing and Agent Turn.

grades.reason: Both prohibit post-placement funding, require one Agent/icon and prohibit no-icon Agent cards; pre-placement Plot clarification agrees with summary.

grades.question: At a Combat space you recruit three troops this turn and already have four garrisoned. How many can deploy? What if the destination is not a Combat space, and where do recruited troops originate?
grades.expected: May deploy all three newly recruited plus at most two older garrison troops, five total. Normal deployment unavailable at noncombat space. Recruit from own supply into garrison; empty supply prevents recruiting.

observed.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all 3 troops recruited that turn plus up to 2 of the 4 already in your garrison, for up to 5. At a non-Combat space normal deployment is not permitted. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.
observed.evidence: Actions: Recruiting & Deploying Units; Board Space Guide Combat? column.

grades.reason: Both give five maximum, no normal noncombat deployment and supply-to-garrison recruitment; empty-supply elaboration is not a separately requested scenario.

grades.question: How do you use a Spy Agent icon, Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence? Can the same Spy pay for both, and when must Gather Intelligence be chosen?
grades.expected: Spy Agent icon permits a connected space without recalling Spy. Infiltrate recalls own connected Spy to bypass another player Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls own connected Spy to draw, chosen immediately after placement before card/space effects. Same Spy cannot do both; separate Spies can.

observed.answer: A Spy Agent icon permits an Agent at a space connected to an observation post where your Spy currently is, without recalling it; the card still needs that icon for this access. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to bypass another player's Agent, not your own. Gather Intelligence may recall a connected Spy to draw one card; choose immediately after placement and before space/card effects, and it allows at most one draw per placement. The same Spy cannot pay both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, though two different Spies can serve the two effects.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Infiltrate, Gather Intelligence, Separate Spy costs and Spy Agent access.

grades.reason: Both distinguish Spy-icon access, Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, including recall costs, separate Spies and immediate decision timing.

grades.question: With two troops, one sandworm and four revealed swords, what is your strength? What if your final unit is removed? Can you participate in Combat Intrigue with no unit?
grades.expected: Strength 11 (2+2+3+4). No units means zero strength regardless swords. Without a unit cannot participate in Combat Intrigue.

observed.answer: Strength is 2 troops×2 + 1 sandworm×3 + 4 swords = 11. If your last Conflict unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you cannot participate in Combat Intrigue.
observed.evidence: Actions: Strength; Phase 3 Combat Intrigue.

grades.reason: Both calculate 11 strength, zero on last-unit loss and no unitless Combat Intrigue.

grades.question: If you pass Combat Intrigue and an opponent then plays one, may you act again? When does the window close, and where do troops and sandworms go after rewards?
grades.expected: May act again after earlier pass; closes only when all involved players pass consecutively. Adjust strength for effects. After all rewards troops return to supply not garrison, sandworms to bank, Combat markers reset zero.

observed.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting later in the window; it closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply, sandworms to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
observed.evidence: Phase 3: Combat; Resolve Combat cleanup.

grades.reason: Both permit acting after a pass, require consecutive passes, and give all cleanup destinations and marker reset; strength updates are not separately asked.

grades.question: Compare two players tied for first in a four-player Conflict with the same tie in a three-player Conflict. Who takes the Conflict card, and can a zero-strength player get a reward?
grades.expected: Each tied first gets second reward and nobody wins or takes card. In four-player game remaining players compete for third; in three-player game no further rewards. Zero strength never rewarded.

observed.answer: In four players, two tied for first each take the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, and nobody takes the Conflict card because there is no winner. In three players, the two tied for first each take second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Combat ties; Resolve Combat.

grades.reason: Both give second rewards, four-player third competition versus no three-player remainder, no card and zero-strength exclusion.

grades.question: What does a sandworm do to rewards: do two sandworms quadruple them, can control or battle icons double, and how is a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP handled?
grades.expected: One or more sandworms doubles, never quadruples. Control and battle icons do not double. Optional reward cost may be paid second time: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2, not free second VP.

observed.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. For an optional cost reward, pay the cost a second time to receive it a second time: a 3-spice-for-1-VP offer can be taken twice by paying 6 spice for 2 VP.
observed.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling.

grades.reason: Both limit doubling to once, exclude control/icons and require paying 6 spice for two VP.

grades.question: When is a normal battle-icon match checked, which cards qualify, is matching optional, and how is a wild icon used?
grades.expected: After winning and taking Conflict card face up in supply check another face-up Conflict or Objective with same icon; must flip pair face down for 1 VP. At Endgame wild can match any of three icons in supply, pair flipped for 1 VP.

observed.answer: After winning and taking a Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. A matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP. At Endgame the wild icon can match any one of the three battle icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
observed.evidence: Battle Icons.

grades.reason: Both give post-acquisition face-up supply check, eligible cards, mandatory pair for 1 VP and Endgame wild use.

grades.question: What are the rewards and reversibility at 2 and 4 Faction Influence, and does tying the Alliance holder at 4 steal the Alliance?
grades.expected: Reach 2 gets 1 VP lost below 2. Reach 4 gets track bonus retained if falling below, can earn again on re-reaching. First to 4 gets Alliance and its VP; tie does not steal, opponent must rise higher. Transfer loses old holder VP and gives new holder VP.

observed.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP, lose it below 2, and regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is kept if you fall below 4 and earned again on returning; the first to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP, which remains only while holding it. Tying the holder does not steal the Alliance; a challenger must rise above them. The separate FAQ trigger for a holder losing Influence after a tie is described in Q38.
observed.evidence: Scoring: Faction Influence.

grades.reason: Both distinguish reversible 2-Influence VP, retained/repeatable track bonus and Alliance-linked VP, with no theft on a tie. A's reference to Q38 is unnecessary and supplies no borrowed facts.

grades.question: When can Persuasion be spent during Reveal, may it be pooled or split, can you buy a Row replacement immediately, and where does the acquired card go?
grades.expected: Before between or after Reveal effects; can pool and split. Refill Row to five immediately; may buy replacement with remaining Persuasion. Acquired card face-up discard, cannot use immediately; unspent Persuasion lost.

observed.answer: During Reveal, Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. Pool sources to buy one card or split a source across cards; unused Persuasion is lost. The Imperium Row refills to five, and you may buy a replacement immediately if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.
observed.evidence: Acquiring Cards.

grades.reason: Both answer spending timing, pooling/splitting, replacement acquisition and face-up discard destination; B's omission of unasked Persuasion expiration is not material.

grades.question: How do Maker bonus spice, the Shield Wall and Maker Hooks affect harvesting and summoning, and where can a sandworm be placed?
grades.expected: Makers phase adds one bonus spice on each unoccupied Maker space, accumulating; visiting collects all bonus spice. Shield Wall blocks worms at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, Imperial Basin until removed to box. Maker Hooks prerequisite when specified; summoning directly bank to Conflict, never garrison.

observed.answer: At Makers, each unoccupied Maker space gains 1 bonus spice; visiting a Maker space collects all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, 2 worms; Hagga costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, 1 worm. Worms go directly into your own Conflict quadrant, never a garrison. Hooks are required only when the effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. The Shield Wall blocks worm summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin until removed.
observed.evidence: Phase 4: Makers; Actions: Sandworms; Board Space Guide.

grades.reason: Both give bonus-spice addition/collection, protected locations, conditional retained Hooks and direct Conflict placement; added harvesting costs/options agree with summary.

grades.question: At what point does 10 VP or an empty Conflict deck end play, what happens before comparing final VP, and what are the rulebook resource tiebreakers?
grades.expected: Check in Recall at end of round, not immediately at 10 VP. Resolve Endgame Intrigue first then highest VP wins. Ties spice then Solari then water then garrisoned troops.

observed.answer: Endgame triggers at the end of a round if anyone has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
observed.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions.

grades.reason: Both identify end-of-round trigger, Endgame Intrigue before VP and correct ordered resource tiebreakers.

grades.question: With optional standard CHOAM, how many contracts start face up and face down, which extra cards are added, is Shaddam compulsory, and are the 10 contrasting-back contracts part of this standard setup?
grades.expected: 20 standard contracts: two face up, eighteen in bank. Add four Intrigue and four Imperium; Shaddam optional. Ten contrasting-back contracts are only Rise of Ix compatibility, excluded from standard setup.

observed.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contracts and expose 2 face up; the remaining 18 are face down in the bank. Shuffle 4 additional Intrigue cards into that deck and 4 additional Imperium cards into that deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are Rise of Ix compatibility cards and stay in the box for standard CHOAM.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module: Setup changes; Components.

grades.reason: Both give the 20-contract standard setup, two offers/18 bank, added cards, optional Shaddam and excluded compatibility set; the question does not posit choosing Shaddam.

grades.question: Under CHOAM, what does the contract icon do, what if all contracts are taken, and how are Harvest, Immediate and Acquire The Spice Must Flow contracts completed?
grades.expected: With CHOAM, take one of the available face-up contracts on the board into your supply, then replace it face up from the bank if a bank contract remains. The printed icon guide gives 2 Solari if there are none left; this does not require every contract token in the game to have been acquired. In particular, another human with no public contract available gains 2 Solari even if Shaddam's set-aside Sardaukar contracts remain unacquired, and cannot take those reserved contracts. Without CHOAM the icon also gives 2 Solari. Shaddam's own reserved-contract option follows Sardaukar Commander and the FAQ. A Harvest contract completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the specified total spice during that turn, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when that card is next acquired.
grades.source_references: See benchmark-v17/source-reference-appendix.json: original main PDF pp16,20, Uprising Board Space Guide, original Shaddam Leader and official FAQ p3, exact named-file/hash locators.

observed.answer: With CHOAM, a contract icon takes an available face-up public contract and refills the offer from the bank if possible; without CHOAM it gives 2 Solari. If no public contracts remain, gain 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the stated spice total during that turn; Immediate completes when taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module: Taking contracts; Completing contracts; Human contract icon.

grades.reason: Both give taking a public offer, replenishment if possible, 2-Solari exhausted-offer fallback and all three completion triggers. A's public-offer/turn-total wording reasonably conveys public availability and total-turn Harvest; unposed reserved-contract and no-module branches need not all be recited.

grades.question: You gain a board-space contract after already sending your Agent to that space this turn. Can you complete it now? Once completed what do you announce, gain and do with the token?
grades.expected: Cannot complete now; must have held contract when Agent sent, wait future turn. Announce completion, gain printed rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

observed.answer: No. You must have held a space contract when you sent the Agent, so one acquired after already visiting that space waits until a future turn. On completion, announce it, gain its rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module: Completing contracts; FAQ: Contract completion is mandatory.

grades.reason: Both prohibit retroactive completion and give prior ownership, future turn, announcement, reward and face-down supply retention.

grades.question: In standard two-player play how many Rivals are used, who gets the Ornithopter Objective, who gets First Player, what is the turn order, and does a Rival Reveal?
grades.expected: One shared Rival. Rival gets Ornithopter Objective, other two randomly humans; Rival never First Player. Marker alternates humans, Rival considered clockwise from First Player and acts between humans each round. Takes Agent turns while it has Agent in supply, never Reveals.

observed.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It receives the Ornithopter Objective; the two humans receive random other eligible Objectives. First Player is the human whose Objective bears the marker, and the marker alternates between humans. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Agent turns.

grades.reason: Both give one Rival, Ornithopter allocation, human First Player/alternation, intervening Rival turn and no Reveal; B need not recite unasked human Objective randomization.

grades.question: A Rival reveals an occupied board space, then a Place Spy card. How does it proceed, which space costs and effects apply, and what happens when House Hagal is empty or Reshuffle is drawn?
grades.expected: Occupied: ignore and reveal again. Place Spy tries empty designated post, ignore placement if none, then reveal another card regardless because no Agent sent. Ignore normal space costs/effects; use Hagal effects only. Empty deck or Reshuffle: immediately reshuffle Hagal and continue.

observed.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of its specified type, otherwise ignore placement, then reveal another card. Ignore ordinary board-space costs and effects and apply only Hagal effects. If the Hagal deck empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Place Spy cards.

grades.reason: Both fully give occupied-space redraw, specified empty Spy post or skip, continued draw, Hagal-only costs/effects and immediate reshuffle.

grades.question: How are eligible Objective cards selected and distributed in standard three- or four-player setup, how is First Player chosen, and may Shaddam be chosen without CHOAM?
grades.expected: Omit Objectives whose 1–3P or 4/6P mark mismatches count; shuffle, each takes one random face up in supply. First Player is holder of marked Objective. Shaddam cannot be chosen without CHOAM.

observed.answer: For 3–4 players, omit Objectives marked for other player counts, shuffle the eligible cards, and give each player one face up; the one showing the First Player marker determines First Player. Shaddam may be chosen only when using CHOAM.
observed.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5.

grades.reason: Both filter player-count markings, shuffle/deal one face up, use marked Objective for First Player and exclude Shaddam without CHOAM.

grades.question: If the bank runs out of Solari, spice, water or sandworms, what happens? Contrast an empty personal troop supply, and state where resource payments go.
grades.expected: Bank resources and sandworms not limited; substitute conveniently. Cannot recruit troops from empty personal supply until returned. Resource gains come from bank and payments return to bank.

observed.answer: Solari, spice, water, and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if the bank runs out. If your troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Payments of Solari, spice, or water return to the bank.
observed.evidence: Setup step 7; Recruiting & Deploying Units.

grades.reason: Both contrast unlimited bank substitutes with finite personal troops and return payments to bank.

grades.question: State all five round phases in order, when Conflict and hand cards are drawn, and what Recall does if Endgame is not triggered.
grades.expected: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Start reveals top Conflict face up atop previous remaining cards then each draws five. If no Endgame, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise and begin next round (two-player Rival exception).

observed.answer: The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict from the top and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed prior Conflict cards; then each player draws five cards. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans First Player passes clockwise, while in 2P Rival Agents return to supply and First Player passes to the other human.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: five phases; Phase 1; Phase 5.

grades.reason: Both give all five phases, Round Start reveal/draw-five and non-Endgame Recall procedures with two-player exception; start of next round is explicit in B and conveyed by A's round sequence.

grades.question: May you resolve board-space effects, Agent-box effects and Faction Influence in any order? Can you use that visit’s Influence to meet its entry requirement?
grades.expected: Resolve effects in any order after placement, but entry requirements and costs must be met before any effects. Cannot rely on Influence gained by the visit for its entry requirement.

observed.answer: Yes, board-space, Agent-box, and Faction Influence effects may be carried out in any order. Entry costs and requirements must be met before resolving any space or played-card effects, so the visit's Influence cannot satisfy that same visit's entry requirement.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent Turn.

grades.reason: Both permit effect ordering only after satisfying entry requirements and reject using the visit's Influence for its entry.

grades.question: Can an optional arrow cost be paid twice in an Agent turn? Which effects are normally optional or mandatory, including costs on Intrigue cards?
grades.expected: Only once per turn, except sandworm-doubled Conflict rewards. Most effects mandatory except may, optional arrow payment and black-X trash. Direct self-trash mandatory. All Intrigue conditions/costs required to play it.
grades.source_references: Main pp9,20; FAQ p3 optional effects/paying a cost

observed.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect can be used only once per turn; sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward is the exception. Most card and space effects are mandatory, while “may,” optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon are exceptions; direct self-trash instructions are mandatory. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play the Intrigue.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ: Mandatory effects and costs.

grades.reason: Both prohibit repeated arrow use, identify doubled Conflict exception, mandatory default/optional exceptions and required Intrigue costs. B does not separately recite self-trash, but identifies the optional trash exception specifically as black-X, with other effects under the mandatory default.

grades.question: Where may a new Spy be placed, what if all your Spies are already deployed, and what if its placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type?
grades.expected: Unoccupied observation post, from supply. If none in supply may first recall one of own Spies for no effect. Specified icon must connect to post or cannot place there.

observed.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of yours for no effect. If the effect specifies an Agent-icon type connected to the post, that connection is required; otherwise the Spy cannot be placed.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts.

grades.reason: Both give unoccupied supply placement, no-effect recall on supply exhaustion and required icon connection.

grades.question: Can you Infiltrate your own occupied board space, use a Spy without playing a card, or recall two connected Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement?
grades.expected: No to all. Infiltrate bypasses another player Agent; still play a card and meet entry costs/requirements. Two Spies can pay different effects (Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence), not duplicate Gather Intelligence.

observed.answer: No, Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent. A Spy does not provide a free Agent turn: you must play a card with matching normal Agent access or Spy Agent access and pay entry costs. You cannot recall two Spies to get two Gather Intelligence draws on one placement; at most one draw is allowed.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence; FAQ: Spies.

grades.reason: Both reject own-Agent Infiltrate, cardless placement and double Gather Intelligence; A also explicitly retains entry costs.

grades.question: Who gets control bonuses when visiting Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin, how is control transferred, and where does the defensive troop originate?
grades.expected: Winning respective Conflict puts control marker on flag replacing opponent. Controller receives 1 Solari at Arrakeen/Refinery or 1 spice at Basin whenever anyone including self visits. Reveal of controlled location Conflict permits one troop from supply directly to Conflict.

observed.answer: The controller gets the location bonus whenever any player, including themself, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. A critical Conflict winner places their Control marker, replacing any opponent's marker. When that Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Critical Locations & Control.

grades.reason: Both give controller bonuses including self-visits, winning-Conflict control replacement and optional supply-to-Conflict defensive troop.

grades.question: When two players tie for second in a three-player Conflict, what happens? What if players tie for third in four-player play, or three players tie for first?
grades.expected: Tied second each get third reward; winner keeps first and card, no other rewards. Tied third receive nothing. Three tied first each get second, no winner/card and no further rewards.

observed.answer: For a second-place tie, each tied player receives the third reward; the first-place winner keeps the first reward and card, and no further rewards are given. A third-place tie gets nothing. Three tied for first each receive second reward; nobody else receives a reward and no one takes the Conflict card.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Combat ties and Three tied for first.

grades.reason: Both correctly resolve ties for second, third and three tied first, including rewards, winner/card and no remaining reward.

grades.question: At a normal three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, which places receive rewards? What if a two-player game’s Rival is one of the participants?
grades.expected: Only first and second rewarded, third only used for a tie for second. Two humans plus standard Rival use the same two-/three-player reward rules; Rival competes normally.
grades.source_references: Main p14; Supplements p5 Combat; FAQ p1 Conflict

observed.answer: In a three-player game, the top two positive strengths receive first and second rewards; the third place receives nothing. The same applies in a two-human game with its Rival as the third competitor: the Rival is a normal scoring participant, and third reward is used only in a tie for second.
observed.evidence: Resolve Combat: player-count rewards; Required Rival Rules.

grades.reason: Both restrict ordinary rewards to first/second and apply the same rules with a Rival; both reserve third reward for a second-place tie.

grades.question: When can Plot, Combat and Endgame Intrigues be played, how are unplayed Intrigues kept and ordinary ones discarded, and what if the Intrigue deck is exhausted?
grades.expected: Plot during own Agent/Reveal turns, Combat during Combat with a unit, Endgame at game end. Unplayed face down separate from deck, owner may inspect; played resolved cards face up Intrigue discard. Exhaustion reshuffles Intrigue discard into new deck.
grades.source_references: Main p7 / extraction 345–354; FAQ p2 Intrigue cards

observed.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played on your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues during Combat only if you have a unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when played; resolved cards go face up in a discard pile beside the Intrigue Deck. If the deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Intrigue cards; FAQ: Draw timing.

grades.reason: Both give all three timing windows, Combat unit restriction, face-down separate storage, face-up Intrigue discard and exhaustion reshuffle; inspection permission is unasked background.

grades.question: Can you discard an Intrigue for an ordinary discard instruction? Where does an ordinary discard come from? How does Secrets choose which Intrigue is stolen?
grades.expected: Ordinary discard from hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified. Secrets steals one random Intrigue from each opponent with four or more, in addition to drawing one from deck and gaining Bene Gesserit Influence.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1104–1106,1179–1181; Supplements p2; FAQ p2 discard

observed.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from hand and cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from hand. Secrets gives one Intrigue selected at random by each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Discarding; Intrigue cards.

grades.reason: Both restrict ordinary discard to non-Intrigue hand cards and give random theft from each opponent at four or more. Unasked Secrets draw/Influence need not be recited.

grades.question: Which cards may a trash effect remove, where do ordinary and Reserve cards go, and is trashing optional? Does trashing The Spice Must Flow remove its acquired VP?
grades.expected: May trash own hand, discard or in-play card. Ordinary to box; Reserve back to its Reserve stack. Optional unless cost or direct self-trash. The Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained after trashing.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1185–1190; FAQ p4 The Spice Must Flow

observed.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Ordinary trashed cards go to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or told to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow's acquire VP remains even if the card is later trashed.
observed.evidence: Trashing; FAQ: Victory.

grades.reason: Both give all three trash origins, distinct box/Reserve destinations, optionality exceptions and retained acquired VP.

grades.question: When do acquire-box effects resolve, when do you reshuffle your deck, and can unused Persuasion be carried to another round?
grades.expected: Acquire effect once at acquisition not when later played. Reshuffle discard only when unable to draw due to empty deck then continue. Unspent Reveal Persuasion lost, never saved.

observed.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once when acquiring the card. If you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Persuasion cannot be saved; unused Persuasion is lost at the end of Reveal.
observed.evidence: Acquiring Cards; Special Rules: Acquire box.

grades.reason: Both give acquisition-time single trigger, draw-needed empty-deck reshuffle and no saved Persuasion.

grades.question: What counts as in play for Fremen Bond, can two Bond cards activate one another regardless of play order, and when do they cease being in play?
grades.expected: Agent-turn and Reveal cards remain in play face up until Reveal Clean Up unless trashed earlier. Bond requires at least one other Fremen in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order.

observed.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed on your Reveal turn are in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order. They cease being in play at Clean Up.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: In play / Fremen Bond.

grades.reason: Both define Agent/Reveal in-play lifetime, other-Fremen requirement, mutual activation regardless of order and cleanup/earlier-trash endpoint.

grades.question: Can Recall Agent return the Agent placed this turn, and when can the recalled Agent act again? Where does a retreated troop go, and may “retreat any number” mean zero?
grades.expected: Recall another Agent from board to Leader, not current-turn Agent; can use on later Agent turn same round. Retreat Conflict to garrison; any number permits zero.
grades.source_references: Main p20 / extraction 1147–1157; FAQ p3 Retreat

observed.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the one just placed; it can act again on a later Agent turn that round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” permits zero.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ: Combat and troops.

grades.reason: Both exclude current-turn Agent, permit later same-round reuse and return retreated troops to garrison with zero allowed.

grades.question: When an effect grants two Influence with a freely chosen Faction, may it be split? What is required for an Alliance-icon effect or a minimum-Influence effect?
grades.expected: Choose one Faction, both Influence there (not split). Alliance effect requires holding shown Faction Alliance token; minimum-Influence effect requires at least shown value with shown Faction.

observed.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence must apply both to one chosen Faction, not split across factions. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token; an effect with a minimum-Influence requirement requires meeting the stated threshold.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Influence.

grades.reason: Both prohibit splitting two Influence and require the matching Alliance token or stated Faction threshold.

grades.question: If an Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, who receives the token? If the holder drops to 3 and no one has 4, what happens?
grades.expected: Former holder chooses one of previously tied opponents to receive token; holder loses Alliance VP and receiver gains it. Below 4 loses token; if no eligible 4+ player return token to board, losing its VP.

observed.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if several were tied, the former holder chooses the recipient. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the Alliance token to the board and the former holder loses its VP.
observed.evidence: Scoring: Faction Influence; FAQ: Alliance loss.

grades.reason: Both identify former holder's choice among tied opponents and return-to-board/lost-VP outcome at 3 with nobody at 4. B additionally states transfer VP; A's unasked transfer bookkeeping is not a requested-part omission.

grades.question: What happens to a card drawn during Reveal compared with one drawn after Reveal? What happens to a Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal?
grades.expected: During Reveal immediately reveal and use this turn; after Reveal keep until next round, then draw five extra. Plot effect for later Reveal stays face up until that Reveal, use then discard.

observed.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards drawn then. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until Reveal, is used then, and is discarded afterward.
observed.evidence: FAQ: Draw timing.

grades.reason: Both distinguish immediate Reveal use from next-round retained card plus five and delayed Plot face-up duration/discard.

grades.question: May a “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue be played after tying for first? What if you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win?
grades.expected: Tie for first is not a win, cannot play. An appropriate Intrigue received as winning reward can be played immediately.
grades.source_references: FAQ p4 When you win a Conflict

observed.answer: No, “when you win” Intrigues cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
observed.evidence: FAQ: Combat and troops.

grades.reason: Both reject win Intrigue on a first-place tie and permit immediate use of one gained from an outright win.

grades.question: What if final VP, spice, Solari, water and garrison troops all remain tied, and may scores exceed 12?
grades.expected: Final tiebreaker is player who most recently took Reveal turn. Scores may exceed printed track maximum 12.
grades.source_references: FAQ p2 Endgame; p4 Victory Points

observed.answer: If VP and all four listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.
observed.evidence: FAQ: Victory.

grades.reason: Both give most recent Reveal as final tiebreaker and permit scores above 12.

grades.question: Can you delay completion of two held contracts for the same board space after visiting, and when in the Agent turn can their effects resolve?
grades.expected: Completion mandatory; all same-space contracts completed with one Agent placement. Their effects may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects; still must hold them at placement.

observed.answer: No. Fulfill all held contracts for a space with the same Agent placement; you cannot delay them after visiting. A contract is another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects, but it must have been held when sending the Agent.
observed.evidence: FAQ: Contract completion is mandatory.

grades.reason: Both require simultaneous held-contract completion and permit ordering with Agent/space effects while preserving ownership at placement.

grades.question: Under CHOAM does Shaddam begin with his set-aside Sardaukar contracts, when can he take one, and how long does his Signet Ring deployment restriction last?
grades.expected: No, not in possession at start. Sardaukar Commander allows acquiring set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of generally available one when taking a contract. Emperor of Known Universe restriction starts immediately with Signet Ring Agent placement and lasts that turn only.
grades.source_references: Main p17; FAQ p3 Shaddam Corrino IV

observed.answer: Shaddam does not start with the two reserved Sardaukar contracts; they are set aside before the initial shuffle. Only he may acquire them, choosing one instead of a generally available contract. His Signet Ring deployment restriction takes effect immediately when played to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the full round.
observed.evidence: CHOAM Module: Setup changes; Reserved Sardaukar contracts; FAQ: Shaddam.

grades.reason: Both exclude starting possession, give Shaddam's reserved alternative acquisition and immediate turn-only restriction.

grades.question: For Feyd, where does the Training token start and what happens at its last space? Which Jessica side begins face up and can Reverend Mother Jessica act on the flip turn?
grades.expected: Feyd starts leftmost Training space, stays forever on rightmost once reached. Lady Jessica side starts up, not Reverend Mother. Reverend Mother ability usable on flip turn.
grades.source_references: Main p17 / extraction 957–964; FAQ p3 Reverend Mother Jessica

observed.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost Training track space and remains on the rightmost space after reaching it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Leader clarifications; FAQ.

grades.reason: Both give leftmost Feyd start/rightmost permanence, Lady Jessica starting face and same-turn Reverend Mother use.

grades.question: For Margot and Irulan does moving from 1 to 3 Influence count as reaching 2, can it trigger again later, and does descending through 2 count? Does Clean Up trigger Spacing Guild’s Favor discard ability?
grades.expected: Passing 2 upward counts, can repeat by losing then regaining Influence; descending does not count. Spacing Guild Favor triggers discard from hand, not in-play-to-discard Clean Up.

observed.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2, and it can count again later if you lose Influence and later move up through 2 again. Moving downward through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Leader clarifications.

grades.reason: Both count upward crossing and repeated return, exclude downward crossing and limit Favor's discard trigger to hand discard.

grades.question: State Accept Contract and Dutiful Service’s Agent icons and effects with and without CHOAM, and whether both automatically advance a Faction track.
grades.expected: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade Agent icon: draw one card and resolve a contract icon; it does not automatically gain Faction Influence. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor Agent icon: gain one Emperor Influence and resolve a contract icon. Without CHOAM each contract icon gives 2 Solari. With CHOAM, take an available public face-up contract into your supply and refill from the bank if possible; the icon gives 2 Solari if no such contract remains. For another human, Shaddam's unacquired set-aside Sardaukar contracts are unavailable and do not prevent this fallback when the public supply is empty. Shaddam's reserved-contract acquisition option remains governed by his Leader and the FAQ.
grades.source_references: See benchmark-v17/source-reference-appendix.json: original main PDF pp16,20, Uprising Board Space Guide, original Shaddam Leader and official FAQ p3, exact named-file/hash locators.

observed.answer: Accept Contract is Spice Trade access, no cost, no Combat; always draw a card and resolve the contract icon (without CHOAM gain 2 Solari; with CHOAM take/refill a public contract, or get 2 Solari if offers are exhausted). It gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service is Emperor access, no cost, no Combat; gain 1 Emperor Influence and resolve the same contract icon. It automatically advances Emperor once, not twice; it is a Faction space.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide; Faction status of the contract spaces; shared human contract icon rule.

grades.reason: Both give Spice Trade/card/no automatic Influence versus Emperor/one Influence, and contract effects with/without module and public exhaustion fallback; public-contract refill wording is a reasonable concise equivalent.

grades.question: What do Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station each cost and provide, what Agent icons access them, and which are Combat spaces?
grades.expected: Arrakeen City free, troop and card, controller 1 Solari. Fremkit Fremen free, 1 Fremen Influence and card. Research Station City 2 water, two troops and two cards. All Combat.

observed.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat yes; controller gets 1 Solari, visitor recruits one troop and draws one card. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide — Standard 2–4 Players.

grades.reason: Both give each access icon, cost, all visitor/controller effects and all three Combat statuses.

grades.question: Compare Deep Desert and Hagga Basin’s entry costs, base spice and worm choices. Do you still collect bonus spice when choosing worms, and are Hooks spent?
grades.expected: Deep Desert 3 water, 4 spice OR two worms; Hagga 1 water, 2 spice OR one worm. Both collect all bonus spice even with worms. Worm choice requires Maker Hooks, not spent; cannot summon into Shield-Wall-protected Conflict.
grades.source_references: Supplements pp1–2; Main p10; FAQ p2 Maker hooks

observed.answer: Deep Desert: Spice Trade, 3 water, 4 base spice or (with Hooks) 2 sandworms. Hagga Basin: Spice Trade, 1 water, 2 base spice or (with Hooks) 1 sandworm. Collect all bonus spice at either space even when choosing worms. Hooks are not spent.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide; Actions: Sandworms.

grades.reason: Both give water/base-spice/worm alternatives, Hooks requirement/retention and bonus spice on worm choice. B adds correct Wall qualification; no protected Conflict is posited in the question.

grades.question: For each Sietch Tabr option, state requirements and effects. Do you get a troop when choosing to remove the Shield Wall?
grades.expected: City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, no resource cost. Option one Hooks if needed, one troop, one water; option two one water and may remove wall. Option two gives no troop or Hooks. Combat space.

observed.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Hooks if lacking them, recruit one troop, gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall; it gives no troop.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr.

grades.reason: Both give shared City/2-Fremen/no-cost requirements, distinct Hooks/troop/water versus water/optional-Wall effects and no troop on removal branch.

grades.question: How do High Council’s first and subsequent visits differ, what does each cost, when is its ongoing benefit used, and is it a Combat space?
grades.expected: Landsraad 5 Solari each visit. First Councilor to empty seat, +2 Persuasion each Reveal rest of game; later 2 spice, Intrigue, three troops. Not Combat, cannot normally deploy recruited troops.

observed.answer: High Council is Landsraad access, costs 5 Solari on each visit, and is not a Combat space. First visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gives 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council.

grades.reason: Both give first/repeat visit distinction, 5-Solari each, ongoing +2 Reveal Persuasion, revisit rewards and noncombat status.

grades.question: What does Swordmaster cost before and after anyone obtains one, how often may each player visit, and when can the new Agent be used? Does a Rival obtaining it lower human cost?
grades.expected: Landsraad 8 Solari before any Swordmaster, then 6; once per player per game. Third Agent from beside board onto Leader immediately usable same round and rest of game. Rival also lowers cost.

observed.answer: Swordmaster is Landsraad access, not Combat. It costs 8 Solari before anyone gains a Swordmaster and 6 afterward; once per player per game. Take the third Agent onto your Leader, available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining one also lowers human cost to 6.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster.

grades.reason: Both give 8-to-6 cost, once per player, current-round/permanent new Agent use and Rival cost reduction.

grades.question: State Imperial Privilege’s Agent icon, requirement, entry cost and effects. Which Agent can it recall and does it automatically give Emperor Influence?
grades.expected: Landsraad, 2+ Emperor Influence, 3 Solari. May discard Intrigue to draw Intrigue; recall another Agent and draw card. Not the current Agent. No automatic Emperor Influence.

observed.answer: Imperial Privilege is Landsraad access, not Combat; costs 3 Solari and requires 2+ Emperor Influence. You may discard an Intrigue to draw one; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege.

grades.reason: Both give Landsraad/2 Emperor/3 Solari, optional Intrigue swap, other-Agent recall/card and no automatic Emperor gain.

grades.question: State Shipping’s access icon, Influence requirement, cost and gains. Does its free-choice Influence have to be with the Guild?
grades.expected: Spice Trade, 2+ Guild Influence, 3 spice. Gain 5 Solari and one Influence any one Faction, not necessarily Guild.

observed.answer: Shipping is Spice Trade access, not Combat; costs 3 spice and requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence. Gain 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; it need not be Guild.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping.

grades.reason: Both give Spice Trade/2 Guild/3 spice, 5 Solari and freely chosen one-Faction Influence.

grades.question: Compare Gather Support and Spice Refinery’s zero-cost and paid options and Combat status.
grades.expected: Gather Support Landsraad choose 0/2 Solari, two troops either way, plus one water if paid, not Combat. Refinery City choose 0/1 spice, gain 2/4 Solari respectively, controller 1 Solari either way, Combat.

observed.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad, not Combat: choose 0 or 2 Solari to recruit two troops; paying 2 also gives 1 water. Spice Refinery is City, Combat: choose 0 or 1 spice to gain 2 or 4 Solari respectively; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide: Gather Support; Spice Refinery.

grades.reason: Both fully distinguish zero/paid options, quantities, controller bonus and Combat statuses.

grades.question: State Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar’s entry costs, Influence gains, recruits and other effects; which allow normal deployment?
grades.expected: Heighliner 5 spice, Guild Influence +1 and five troops, Combat. Desert Tactics 1 water, Fremen Influence +1 and one troop, optional trash, Combat. Sardaukar 4 spice, Emperor Influence +1 and four troops plus Intrigue, not Combat.

observed.answer: Heighliner: Guild access, costs 5 spice, gain 1 Guild Influence and recruit 5; Combat yes. Desert Tactics: Fremen, costs 1 water, gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit 1, optionally trash a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar: Emperor, costs 4 spice, gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue, recruit 4; Combat no.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

grades.reason: Both give all three costs, matching Influence, recruit quantities, ancillary effects and deployment statuses.

grades.question: What are Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies’s Agent icons, costs and effects, including Assembly Hall’s timing condition?
grades.expected: Assembly Hall Landsraad free, Intrigue now, 1 Persuasion at Reveal if own Agent there. Espionage BG 1 spice, 1 BG Influence, card and Spy. Deliver Supplies Guild free, 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. None Combat.

observed.answer: Assembly Hall: Landsraad, no cost, not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage: Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild, no cost, not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
observed.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

grades.reason: Both give all icons, costs/effects and Assembly Hall's Reveal-with-Agent condition; added noncombat statuses agree.

grades.question: What must False Orders’ affected opponents do, may it be played without an opposing Spy connected to your destination, and when is Litany Against Fear’s red box ignored?
grades.expected: Each affected opponent moves Spy to empty observation post not connected to this turn Agent destination. Can play without enemy Spy there. Litany red box ignored during Reveal or with gained Agent icon when played normally as Agent card.
grades.source_references: FAQ pp2–3 False Orders/Litany Against Fear

observed.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
observed.evidence: FAQ: Leader/card rulings.

grades.reason: Both give empty disconnected Spy destination, play without enemy Spy there and both red-box exceptions.

grades.question: With Manipulate, may opponents acquire the removed card, may you acquire it by other means with the discount, and when does an unacquired card leave the game?
grades.expected: Opponents cannot acquire. You may use other means but 1-Persuasion discount does not apply. If not acquired by end of next Reveal turn, remove from game.

observed.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it has not been acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
observed.evidence: FAQ: Manipulate.

grades.reason: Both prohibit opponent acquisition, remove discount for alternate acquisition and expire at end of next Reveal.

grades.question: What components and resource does the standard two-player Rival start with, what happens to the 2P Reshuffle card, and can its 10 VP trigger Endgame and victory?
grades.expected: Four cubes at Influence bottoms, three garrison troops rest supply, two Agents supply and third beside board, three Spies and one water supply, score/Combat zero. Retain Reshuffle in Hagal. Scoring Rival can trigger end at 10+ and win.

observed.answer: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes, 3 troops in garrison and 9 in supply, 2 Agents in supply and the third beside the board, 3 Spies, 1 water, and score and Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival is a scoring competitor; its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Rival starting components.

grades.reason: Gives the quantities, troop/Agent destinations, marker zeroes, Reshuffle and scoring threat, but only says 'four Influence cubes' without placing them at the bottoms of the four Faction tracks.

grades.question: When does a Rival buy Swordmaster, how does it count and prioritize spending resources, does it keep leftovers, and is its Agent available immediately?
grades.expected: As soon as total resources reaches printed value; Solari spice Intrigues water each unit one. Spend only threshold, prioritizing Solari then spice then Intrigue then water; keep leftovers. Third Agent immediately available including current round.
grades.source_references: Supplements p5; p2 Swordmaster; FAQ p3 Rivals

observed.answer: As soon as its Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water total reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends exactly that many and takes its third Agent, usable that round. Count each unit/resource/card as one. Mandatory spending order is Solari, spice, Intrigue, water; use each type fully as needed before the next, stopping at cost and keeping leftovers. The Agent is immediately usable.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Swordmaster resource total and spending priority.

grades.reason: Both give immediate threshold purchase, all counted resource types at one each, mandatory priority, exact threshold spend/leftovers and current-round Agent availability.

grades.question: After a Rival has Swordmaster, which exact resource sets does it spend for VP, and can it spend a mixed total of seven resources for a VP?
grades.expected: Each set 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigues or 3 water gives 1 VP whenever available. No mixed seven-resource VP purchase; mixed total only used for Swordmaster.
grades.source_references: Supplements p5 Buying Victory Points diagram

observed.answer: After Swordmaster, spend each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. A mixed total of seven does not qualify; only the exact listed sets do.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: After Swordmaster.

grades.reason: Both give exact separate VP sets and reject mixing unlike resources.

grades.question: When choosing Influence, how does a Rival select the Faction and break ties? Does it get VP at 2 and Alliance VP, or the track bonus at 4? What does a numbered Hagal Influence icon mean?
grades.expected: Choose least Influence, ties leftmost priority. Gains/losses of Influence VP and Alliance VP as humans, no 4-track bonus. Number means Faction at that position in printed priority list.

observed.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by the leftmost priority icon. It gains VP for reaching 2 and Alliance VP like a human, but gets no resource bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in its Faction priority list.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: After Swordmaster; Rival turns; Combat.

grades.reason: Both give least-Influence/leftmost-priority choice, 2/Alliance VP but no 4 resource bonus, and numbered priority-list interpretation.

grades.question: A Rival reveals a two-destination Hagal card and the condition-selected destination is occupied. Can it use the other destination, and what conditions select these cards?
grades.expected: Cannot switch to other; reveal again. Accept Contract/Shipping based on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner based on Conflict tier I/II/III. Use card printed condition.
grades.source_references: Supplements p4 Special Instructions; FAQ p3 Rivals

observed.answer: No. Choose only the destination matching the current condition—Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner. If that selected destination is occupied, reveal another Hagal card rather than using the other destination.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns.

grades.reason: Both forbid fallback destination and identify Guild Influence versus Conflict-tier selectors.

grades.question: A Rival has no troops newly recruited by a card sending it to Combat. Can it deploy garrison troops? What if a Hagal card recruits at a noncombat space or has a conditional 2-Influence bonus not met?
grades.expected: Still deploy up to two available garrison troops at Combat. New troops at noncombat go garrison. Missing 2-Influence bonus does not block placement, just no bonus. Use only Hagal effects, not ordinary board effects.

observed.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if that card recruits none. At a noncombat space newly recruited troops go to its garrison. An unmet conditional 2+ Influence bonus is simply omitted and does not prevent Agent placement.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns.

grades.reason: Both allow up to two existing garrison troops without recruitment, put noncombat recruits in garrison and omit unmet bonus without blocking placement. B's 'may' answers the posed capability, not a stated override of automated maximum deployment.

grades.question: How does a Rival choose an unrestricted Spy post, what happens if all Faction posts are occupied, and what occurs on placing its third Spy? Can it Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence?
grades.expected: First available Faction post by priority; if all full ignore placement. Third/final supply Spy placed triggers immediately recalling other two and printed Scheme. Never Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

observed.answer: For an unrestricted placement, use the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing the third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. The Rival never recalls Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes.

grades.reason: Both give priority Faction-post selection, occupied-post skip, immediate third-Spy recall/Scheme and no Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

grades.question: If a Rival’s Scheme recruits troops before a Hagal Agent reaches a Combat space on that same turn, what happens to those troops? What if a Place Spy card found no legal post?
grades.expected: Deploy Scheme recruits on same-turn Combat placement. Place Spy card still followed by another Hagal reveal whether placement succeeds or not, because no Agent has been sent.

observed.answer: Troops recruited by a Scheme before Agent placement can deploy if the Rival visits a Combat space that same turn. If a Place Spy card finds no legal post, ignore placement and reveal another Hagal card because it has not sent an Agent.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards.

grades.reason: Both allow same-turn Scheme recruits to deploy and require redraw after failed Spy placement.

grades.question: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, how does a Rival choose worms versus base spice with Hooks, without Hooks, or with a protected Conflict? What happens to accumulated bonus spice?
grades.expected: Always take bonus spice. With Hooks and summonable Conflict summons one at Hagga/two Deep instead of base. Without Hooks or if protected, summons none and gains base spice (2/4). At Imperial Basin gains base1. Hagal wall removal requires Hooks.

observed.answer: The Rival takes all accumulated bonus spice at the Maker space. At Hagga or Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and the Conflict allows worms, it summons one or two respectively instead of taking base spice; if it summons none, it gets base spice (2 or 4). Without Hooks it takes base spice. A protected Conflict prevents summoning while the Wall remains, so it takes base spice; Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice. Hooks are retained.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Maker spaces; Actions: Sandworms.

grades.reason: Both give mandatory worms with Hooks/legal Conflict, base-spice fallback otherwise, exact 1/2 worms and 2/4 spice, and all accumulated bonus spice.

grades.question: When and how is a Rival’s Combat strength bonus determined, what if Reshuffle appears, and can humans respond afterward? Does a unit-free Rival get this bonus?
grades.expected: Start Combat in turn order, only with deployed unit: one Hagal card, bottom swords only added. Reshuffle and draw again on Reshuffle. Humans then Combat Intrigue before resolution. No unit no bonus.

observed.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal one Hagal card and add its bottom swords to strength; on Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A Rival with no unit gets no such bonus.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Combat.

grades.reason: Both give start-of-Combat Hagal bottom-sword bonus conditional on units, Reshuffle redraw and subsequent human window; B also recites turn order.

grades.question: Can a Rival gain control, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and doubled rewards? How does it handle optional Conflict VP payments and contract rewards with CHOAM?
grades.expected: Normal control visit bonus and defensive supply troop; win card/match icons; sandworms double. Always buy optional Conflict VP if can pay resources or required Spy recall. Never contracts; each contract reward becomes 2 Solari even with CHOAM.

observed.answer: Yes: it gains control bonuses on visits and defensive troops when its controlled Conflict is revealed, wins cards and battle-icon VP normally, and doubles rewards if it has a sandworm. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay/recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari, even with CHOAM.
observed.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Combat.

grades.reason: Both permit all four normal benefits, require affordable optional VP and convert contract rewards to 2 Solari even with module.

grades.question: When during Reveal do you total, announce and set Combat strength, can you update it during the turn, and how is strength over 20 marked?
grades.expected: After Reveal Cards and before Clean Up, at any point while resolving effects; announce total, set marker and update as needed. Above20 flip +20 side and count again from beginning of track.

observed.answer: During Reveal effects, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point; you may update it as strength changes during Reveal. If Combat Intrigue alters units or strength, adjust the marker when that card resolves in the Combat Intrigue window. Strength above 20 uses the +20 side and starts again from the beginning of the track.
observed.evidence: Reveal Turn; Strength; Phase 3: Combat.

grades.reason: Both give flexible Reveal-effects total/announcement/marker update and +20 flip/restart; A's added Combat Intrigue update is supported.

grades.question: When is a Leader’s Signet Ring ability activated, does merely revealing Signet Ring activate it, and can card text override normal game rules?
grades.expected: Activated when playing Signet Ring on an Agent turn, not when merely revealing. Left Leader ability used as described. Cards of any type can override normal rules.

observed.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal that card. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
observed.evidence: Setup step 3; Overview.

grades.reason: Both activate Signet on Agent play rather than Reveal and permit card-rule overrides.

grades.question: How is a Recall Spy icon on a card resolved, where does the Spy go, and is it automatically the same as Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence?
grades.expected: Return one of own Spies from observation post to supply, usually a cost for card effect. Card recall distinct from the two voluntary recalls for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; it does not automatically give either benefit.

observed.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for an effect. It is a separate icon and is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those abilities have their own conditions and timing.
observed.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts; Separate Spy costs.

grades.reason: Both give own-post-to-supply recall and distinguish it from automatic Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence benefits.

grades.question: What does the “trash an Intrigue” icon allow you to choose, as opposed to an ordinary discard-a-card instruction?
grades.expected: Trash an Intrigue of choice from own hand. Ordinary discard chooses a non-Intrigue from hand unless explicitly specified.

grades.question: Can you delay completion of two held contracts for the same board space after visiting, and when in the Agent turn can their effects resolve?

grades.question: What do Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station each cost and provide, what Agent icons access them, and which are Combat spaces?

grades.question: Compare Deep Desert and Hagga Basin’s entry costs, base spice and worm choices. Do you still collect bonus spice when choosing worms, and are Hooks spent?

grades.question: What does Swordmaster cost before and after anyone obtains one, how often may each player visit, and when can the new Agent be used? Does a Rival obtaining it lower human cost?

grades.question: State Imperial Privilege’s Agent icon, requirement, entry cost and effects. Which Agent can it recall and does it automatically give Emperor Influence?

grades.question: What must False Orders’ affected opponents do, may it be played without an opposing Spy connected to your destination, and when is Litany Against Fear’s red box ignored?

grades.question: When does a Rival buy Swordmaster, how does it count and prioritize spending resources, does it keep leftovers, and is its Agent available immediately?
grades.expected: As soon as total resources reaches printed value; Solari spice Intrigues water each unit one. Spend only threshold, prioritizing Solari then spice then Intrigue then water; keep leftovers. Third Agent immediately available including current round.

grades.question: After a Rival has Swordmaster, which exact resource sets does it spend for VP, and can it spend a mixed total of seven resources for a VP?
grades.expected: Each set 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigues or 3 water gives 1 VP whenever available. No mixed seven-resource VP purchase; mixed total only used for Swordmaster.

observed.evidence: After Swordmaster: whenever Rival has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.

grades.reason: Both give exact separate VP sets and reject mixing unlike resources.

grades.question: When choosing Influence, how does a Rival select the Faction and break ties? Does it get VP at 2 and Alliance VP, or the track bonus at 4? What does a numbered Hagal Influence icon mean?
grades.expected: Choose least Influence, ties leftmost priority. Gains/losses of Influence VP and Alliance VP as humans, no 4-track bonus. Number means Faction at that position in printed priority list.

grades.question: A Rival reveals a two-destination Hagal card and the condition-selected destination is occupied. Can it use the other destination, and what conditions select these cards?
grades.expected: Cannot switch to other; reveal again. Accept Contract/Shipping based on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner based on Conflict tier I/II/III. Use card printed condition.

observed.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination card selection and occupied destination.

observed.evidence: Rival Agent turns: recruit/deploy rules; unmet 2+ Influence bonus does not prevent Agent placement.

grades.question: How does a Rival choose an unrestricted Spy post, what happens if all Faction posts are occupied, and what occurs on placing its third Spy? Can it Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence?
grades.expected: First available Faction post by priority; if all full ignore placement. Third/final supply Spy placed triggers immediately recalling other two and printed Scheme. Never Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

observed.answer: When no post type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. observed.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes.

grades.question: If a Rival’s Scheme recruits troops before a Hagal Agent reaches a Combat space on that same turn, what happens to those troops? What if a Place Spy card found no legal post?
grades.expected: Deploy Scheme recruits on same-turn Combat placement. Place Spy card still followed by another Hagal reveal whether placement succeeds or not, because no Agent has been sent.

observed.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Place Spy card behavior.

grades.reason: Both allow same-turn Scheme recruits to deploy and require redraw after failed Spy placement.

grades.question: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, how does a Rival choose worms versus base spice with Hooks, without Hooks, or with a protected Conflict? What happens to accumulated bonus spice?

grades.question: When and how is a Rival’s Combat strength bonus determined, what if Reshuffle appears, and can humans respond afterward? Does a unit-free Rival get this bonus?

If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window and can respond afterward. A Rival with no deployed unit does not get this bonus.
